result:
My verdict for DG5 round 2 is **FAIL**. One required check fails every time on the frozen candidate: the product's own end-to-end test suite cannot pass in Arabic. The product itself behaves correctly; the fault is in a test.

**Candidate.** I confirmed `sha256:5df44203…` (2203 files, source `edbf5ce`) on a complete disposable clone at the start and the end of the review. During my run, the other two reviewers' records were auto-committed. They touch nothing in the candidate, and I did not open them.

**My three round-1 findings are all closed and verified.** Each fix commit is an ancestor of the source, and each fix was re-tested on the real stack in English and Arabic, with the locale unset and set:
- **F-DG5-140:** neither the auditor nor the admin gets the launch form any more, including after a reload or navigating back. Both see the read-only note. The server still refuses the launch (403) and creates nothing. Lead and office still get the form. A build with the permission check removed is caught by both the product test and my probe.
- **F-DG5-141:** the two halves of the split dashboard test take at most 18.2 s of their 60 s budget in both full runs.
- **F-DG5-142:** with a quarter-hour schedule boundary forced between the test's read and the screen's read, A22 passes in all four combinations. A build that shows a stale next run makes A22 fail, so the fix did not weaken the test.

**Checks run**
- **Static:** all 7 checks exit 0.
- **Unit tests:** 4/4 runs exit 0 inside the load limit (peak 6.38). An earlier series had the same results but ran above the limit, so I disclosed it and didn't count it.
- **Integration:** run twice; each time 3084 passed plus 1 intended skip, across migrations 0001–0097. The contract test passes and the pending lists are empty.
- **`tests/qa` alone:** 336/336. The four suites REQ-DLV-037 names pass on this candidate: A06 27, A07 12, A15 34, A16 30.
- **Root and demo acceptance specs:** root 30/30 and demo 12/12 in both locale settings.
- **Probes:** all pass, covering REQ-PB-093 in the Studio UI, the three B0147 traceability chains on the rendered screen, the approval label opened from the inbox, the demo Day-90 test, the provisional label in the executive-pack PDF, and CSV formula injection.
- **Auditor read-only sweep:** 34 P5 screens with zero problems, including the 390 px and 200 % text checks.
- **Validators:** all 6 pass.
- **Exported files:** I inspected 82 files (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and CSV) at content level. Every Arabic file is right-to-left with Arabic fonts, and every file carries the demo label and the B0004 provenance. Rendering them as images isn't possible in this sandbox. I disclosed that as an environmental limit, as in round 1.
- **Product end-to-end suite:**

| Locale setting | Passed | Failed | Did not run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unset | 465 | 2 | 3 |
| C.UTF-8 | 468 | 1 | 1 |

**New findings**
- **F-DG5-143 (Medium, not mandatory, owner frontend-ux-engineer, REQ-S12-012).** `p3-prioritization-roadmap.spec.ts:542` fails in chromium-ar in both full runs and when run alone.
  - **Cause:** the repair wave added a dependency-slips table to the Dependencies page. One column's sort button is labelled «الاعتمادية» ("Dependency"), which contains «اعتماد» ("approve"). The test's write-control pattern `/approve|اعتماد|move|نقل/i` therefore counts a read-only sort control.
  - **Effect:** the next serial test (capacity, Arabic) then doesn't run.
  - **Why it was missed:** the orchestrator skipped the e2e runs before freezing (D-186), so this is the case D-186 itself names as a reason to reopen.
  - **Why it blocks:** a Medium finding can't be accepted as an observation, and the gate needs its required checks to pass.
- **F-DG5-144 (Low, not mandatory, owner frontend-ux-engineer, REQ-S10-012).** `p4-raid-governance.spec.ts:290` (test 5) has no explicit time budget.
  - **Measured:** it timed out at 30.1 s in Arabic in the unset full run, with no failed assertion. It passes alone (16.5–16.9 s) and took 25.0 s in the C.UTF-8 run.
  - **Class:** the same timing problem as F-DG5-141, in a different test.

Every other non-zero exit is explained in `RUN-NOTES.md`. These include my own mistakes: a misnamed A20 path, run separately afterwards; a production-only spec wrongly included in one demo-stack run; a fixture error in my CSV probe; and a run that never started. The record names `reviews/DG4/round-20/qa-verifier.json` as the format to mirror, but that file doesn't exist (DG4 stops at round 10). I followed the schema and my round-1 record instead.

No product file was changed. Probes and the test builds with deliberately broken code ran only in the disposable clone, which is removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-2/`:
- qa-verifier.json
- qa-verifier.verifications.json
- qa-verifier.findings.json
- qa-verifier.md

The evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/qa/round-2/`, starting with `RUN-NOTES.md`.
